_README: Tower Toppler (NTSC), 64K SuperGame + RAM at $4000. Survey annotations, 2026-11-18.
Spaces: f3 = fixed bank ($C000-$FFFF, file bank 3); b0/b1/b2 = file banks 0-2 in the window
(the game writes 4, 5, 6 to select them). Names are the survey's readings: see
docs/parts/towertoppler.md for the evidence tag of each. Coverage is partial: the fixed bank's
display, tower, sprite and frame code was read; game logic (F28E-F9FF), most of bank 2 and all
of banks 0/1 except the tables named here were not.

comments.f3:FECD: bank id: every switched bank ends with its own register value at $BFFF (4, 5, 6), so the NMI saves and restores the bank with no RAM shadow
comments.f3:FEED: $2218 = top window zone's DLL byte ($80 | height-1); +$98 gives CHARBASE $18 + (height-1) for the short last zone, so it shows the top lines of its characters
comments.f3:E6FF: vertical fine scroll: last zone height 2,4,6,8 from (camera y AND 3), top zone gets 9 minus that; then the last zone's sprite slots get graphics page $71 + (top height - 1)
comments.f3:E6C5: the flip: 18 DLL entries' list high bytes, $60.. or $65..; both sets share the low bytes
comments.f3:C4CC: the wall: 16 bytes of bit patterns for this rotation phase from b2:$A200, the same 16 for every other row; the rows between take the phase 4 steps on
comments.f3:C802: b2:$A2D8: relative angle -> x in 2-pixel units (bit 7 = hidden); x/4 is the byte column, x AND 3 picks one of four pre-shifted shapes
comments.f3:C936: one bit per cell, LSB first: set = the next data byte goes into the cell, clear = the cell stays 0
comments.f3:E0AE: b2:$A358: relative angle -> sprite x on the cylinder (bit 7 = behind the tower)
